label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition
explanation: Fires only at D2, and almost only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1 (a rare transition), using only the current inputs (in_action=2, in_state=1). Dev P=0.975, R=0.939, mass recall 0.98. It never fires at D1 or GO, or when S2 is reached. It barely fires on common a1->S1 (about 2% of mass, all weak). Magnitude, from example windows: the strongest activations come when the reward input at that trial D1 was 0 (r0), and they are weaker (about 0.6-0.9 of max) after a rewarded trial. Missed activations sit in the lowest quartile. Adding a strongly negative policy logit (choice < -4.44) raises precision to 0.99 but cuts recall, so the simpler predicate is recorded.

issues: Factual claims check out on dev. The unit has 0 activations at D1 and GO; all of its mass is at D2. Every activation has in_state==1 (S2 never fires). in_action==1 holds 1.8% of the mass. The predicate scores P 0.975 / R 0.939 / mass recall 0.982 on dev, and on test P 0.974 / R 0.929 / F1 0.951.

Misses on test (4285 steps, 2.1% of mass) are almost all common a1->S1 D2 steps at low magnitude (0.03-0.26 of max), in line with the lowest-quartile coverage of 0.76. Restricting to a1->S1 after an unrewarded trial raises the firing rate only to about 9% (P 0.088), so the misses do not form a usable class.

False positives (1470 on test) are rare a2->S1 steps where the unit stays silent. They are somewhat more common when good==S1 (P 0.93 vs 0.99 when good==S2). That is a small effect on precision, not a systematic counterexample class.

The magnitude claim holds roughly. With prev_reward==0, the share of mass (0.39) is above the share of active steps (0.34), so those activations are stronger per step. Within the predicate, firing is nearly unconditional on previous reward: P 0.96 when prev_reward==0, 0.98 when ==1.
The predicate uses only observed inputs (in_action, in_state), so there is no future-variable concern. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
